{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "ULTRA MASTER PROMPT – ARCHITECTURE EDITORIAL DASHBOARD WEBSITE (STATIC ONLY) Create a premium static website for an architecture editorial magazine called “FORM INDEX”. It should feel like Instagram meets Material Design, but for architects, interior designers, urban planners, and design lovers. Build it only with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No backend, no API, no login, no database, no live data. Use mock/static/sample content only. The website must run by opening index.html in a browser.

MAIN IDEA: A visual architecture editorial site presented like a beautiful dashboard / discovery feed. It should combine magazine articles, project cards, architect spotlights, city indexes, moodboards, statistics widgets, and saved-look style panels. It is NOT a social network and must not need real accounts. It just has an Instagram-inspired visual layout: story circles, square image grid, profile-like cards, follow-style buttons as decorative static UI, reels-like vertical feature cards but no video streaming.

STYLE: Material design, clean, modern, editorial, premium, minimal but rich. Use cards, elevation, rounded corners, soft shadows, grid layouts, sticky sections, chips, tabs, bottom navigation on mobile, floating action button, smooth hover transitions, ripple-like button effects using CSS/JS if possible. Color palette: warm off-white background, charcoal text, concrete gray surfaces, terracotta accent, muted sage green, deep ink blue. Use architecture feeling: blueprint lines, grid overlays, column shapes, floorplan patterns, glassmorphism only lightly. Typography should feel editorial: big serif-style headlines if available through system fonts, clean sans-serif for UI. No external fonts required; use safe font stacks.

PAGES / SECTIONS REQUIRED (single page is okay but must feel like multiple dashboard areas):
1. TOP APP BAR: logo FORM INDEX, nav links: Today, Projects, Cities, Studios, Materials, Archive. Include search input visually only with placeholder “Search projects, studios, materials...” no real search backend required, but basic static filtering with JS is welcome.
2. HERO DASHBOARD: large editorial headline “Architecture worth slowing down for.” Include subtext about curated spaces, urban stories, and material studies. Add CTA buttons: Explore Issue, View Project Index. Include a large feature card with an architectural image placeholder/gradient and metrics widgets: 128 featured spaces, 42 cities, 16 material studies.
3. INSTAGRAM-LIKE STORY STRIP: circular story cards with labels: Minimal Homes, Concrete, Adaptive Reuse, Desert Houses, Timber, Museums, Micro Apartments, Public Space. Static only, horizontal scroll on mobile.
4. EDITORIAL FEED: masonry or responsive card grid of at least 12 article/project cards. Each card needs category chip, title, location, short excerpt, fake reading time, image placeholder, and small interaction row with static icons like save/share/view. Example topics: “A courtyard house in Oaxaca”, “Five libraries using light as structure”, “Apartment renovation under 45m²”, “Brutalist campus archive”, “Sage-green kitchen material board”, etc.
5. DASHBOARD ANALYTICS PANEL: static material dashboard widgets showing editorial stats such as Trending Materials, Popular Cities, Weekly Reads, Design Mood Index. Use progress bars, mini charts made with CSS divs/SVG, donut style chart using CSS if possible. Everything is fake/static.
6. FEATURED STUDIO PROFILE: Instagram profile inspired block for an architecture studio: avatar placeholder, studio name, city, bio, fake stats (projects, essays, saves), grid of 6 square thumbnails, tabs: Projects / Notes / Materials. No real follow function, just decorative button.
7. CITY INDEX: cards for Tokyo, Copenhagen, Mexico City, Barcelona, Seoul, São Paulo, Lisbon, Melbourne. Each card includes architecture vibe tags, article count, and a static skyline/floorplan illustration style.
8. MATERIAL LIBRARY: dashboard table/cards for Concrete, Travertine, Cross-laminated timber, Recycled brick, Stainless steel, Limewash, Glass block, Cork. Include color swatches, texture notes, sustainability score, common use, and editorial tag chips.
9. ISSUE OF THE WEEK: long editorial layout with large title, quote block, pull quote, two-column text, and image placeholders. Topic: “The quiet return of human-scale architecture.” Make it feel like a magazine article inside a dashboard.
10. CURATOR PICKS: horizontal carousel-like row using static JS buttons optional. Cards should show editor name, theme, and selected projects. No API, just local array.
11. NEWSLETTER / FOOTER: static newsletter form visually only, maybe prevent default and show small “Demo only” message. Footer links: About, Submissions, Archive, Privacy, Contact. Include note: “Static editorial prototype with sample content.”

INTERACTIONS REQUIRED USING VANILLA JS ONLY: dark/light theme toggle, active nav state on scroll if possible, filter chips for article categories using local static data/classes, simple saved animation when clicking bookmark icon but no persistence needed (localStorage optional but not required), responsive mobile menu, carousel arrows for curator picks, newsletter demo message. Keep everything client-side.

RESPONSIVE REQUIREMENTS: Must look excellent on desktop, tablet, and mobile. Desktop should feel like a complex dashboard with side widgets. Mobile should feel like a premium Instagram/editorial feed with bottom nav and horizontal story strip. Use CSS Grid and Flexbox. Avoid horizontal overflow.

ASSETS: Do not depend on real external image APIs. Use gradients, CSS illustrations, inline SVG patterns, or placeholder blocks that look architectural. If using images, only local placeholder paths or CSS backgrounds. No Unsplash API, no Instagram embed, no external services.

DELIVERABLE: Create a complete static site with index.html, styles.css, script.js. Use semantic HTML, accessible buttons, good contrast, aria labels where useful. The final result should feel complex, polished, realistic, and ready to present as a static architecture editorial dashboard prototype.",
 "judge": {
  "model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8",
  "model_sha": "94125d2bd83076b21eed33119525e29eaf3894f4",
  "request_model": "meta-llama/Llama-4-Maverick-17B-128E-Instruct-FP8:novita",
  "provider": "novita",
  "pinned_on": "2026-10-09",
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "rubric_id": "rva1:mean(visual,query,asset)"
 }
}

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Use temperature zero and bind the model/provider request and artifact revision; mask absent or mismatched deployment/response revision. Version-aware judge endpoint validation is staged.
